newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH FIRMS EXPECT RISING PROFITABILITY - SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH FIRMS EXPECT RISING PROFITABILITY - SURVEY.

text.p: Finnish industrial and service sector companies expect their net sales and profitability to go on rising, according to a financing survey made by employer lobbies, the trade and industry ministry and the central bank.
The spring 1997 survey, released on Wednesday, said companies expected the three-month Helibor interest rate to rise only slightly in the year ahead and they did not expect iflation to accelerate.
In a joint statement, the Confederation of Finnish Industry
and Employers (TT), the Ministry of Trade and Industry (KTM) and
the Bank of Finland said the survey indicated that there would
be hardly any increase in demand for new credits or other forms
of external financing.
Other key points from their statement:
* Corporate sector investments are expected to increase
roughly as much as last autumn and last spring,
* A growing number of companies plan to hire more staff,
* Expectations regarding wages are now for slightly lower
hikes than in the autumn 1996 survey,
* Less than 10 percent of respondents expected weaker
profitability, big companies were somewhat more optimistic than
others,
* EMU expected to bring financial market stability, seen
increasing competition between suppliers of financing services,
* Euro expected to bring clear changes in corporate
financing, effects seen mainly positive.
The survey covered 535 service sector companies and 303
industrial companies.
